title: Agent report
description: What an agent hands back when it finishes one issue: a JSON file the orchestrator queries field by field, plus a path and at most two lines in chat. The orchestrator reads what it needs when it needs it instead of paying for a document on every later turn of the session. Validate with scripts/report_schema.py.
x-honesty: This schema checks SHAPE, never TRUTH. A structured summary is easier to accept without reading than a paragraph is, and that is the trade being made here: a refused disposition renders identically whether the refusal was argued or lazy. Two lists below say which is which. x-enforced is what scripts/report_schema.py actually refuses a report over, and every name in it is paired with a mutation in tests/test_agent_report_schema.py that proves the refusal happens. x-convention is the rest -- real parts of the contract, checked by nobody, and listed here so the next person meets the limit at the same moment they meet the schema.
x-convention: that a survey marked checked was in fact checked -- nothing here can see whether a reviewer ever spawned
that a refusal's reason argues the point rather than restating the finding
that files matches what the commit actually touched
that every claim needing a grade appears in claims, and that the grades are honest
that summary is two lines rather than a document moved one field to the left
that pushed is false, which the contract requires and this validator does not
that the agent writes a report at all -- an agent that ignores this document produces nothing for any assertion to see

head.description: The commit the agent stopped on.

pushed.description: The contract says an agent never pushes. Recorded rather than assumed, so a run that was pushed is visible instead of silent.

summary.description: At most two lines. The whole of what the orchestrator reads before deciding push / review / bounce.

files.description: One entry per file the commit touches, one line each.

claims.description: Claims the run could not observe on the machine it ran on -- platform legs above all. Not every sentence in the report: the set that needs a grade. A run that never assessed them says state not-checked and why, which is different from having none.

blocked.description: Steps that could not be taken -- a permission prompt on a git step, an unspawnable agent, a decision that is not the agent's to make. A permission block is reported, never routed around.

note_path.description: Absolute path to the long half, when one was written. Lives outside every worktree so it can never enter a diff.

split_cost.description: One line: roughly how much went to the note versus the report, and whether anything had to be left out of both. Without it the split is a guess that got adopted.

survey.description: Every list in this report is a survey, because an empty array cannot say whether anyone looked. checked with no items means looked and found nothing. not-checked means nobody looked, and must say why.

scope.description: Where it applies -- a platform, a Python version, a shell.

grade.description: observed: run here. reasoned: argued from the code, worth having, still not run. unobserved: named and not established.

tests.description: One object rather than two, so a run with a green and no red is a stated state instead of a missing key.

state.description: not-applicable is the honest answer for a prose-only change; not-run is the answer when a test should have been watched failing and was not.

mechanism.description: What actually ran, named exactly -- the subagent type and the brief it was pointed at -- or that nothing did. A review that did not execute must never render as a review that found nothing.

classes.description: One verdict per class, always present, so a class nobody reached is visible rather than absent.

findings.description: An empty items list under state checked is a review that ran and found nothing. Under state not-checked it is a review that never ran. Those are not the same value and must never be spelled the same way.

text.description: The finding as the reviewer put it, in full. One sentence is cheap; a boolean is unreadable.

reason.description: Required when the disposition is refused or argued-down: the argument, not a restatement. This is the field that keeps the orchestrator arguing with findings rather than scanning past them.

pr_body.description: The agent writes the pull request body to a file and returns the path; the orchestrator reads it and passes it to the forge. That deletes a translation step that costs a thousand tokens and loses detail on the way. Judgment does not move: the orchestrator still reads the body before it opens anything.

examples.head: 1dc856d
examples.summary: Suffix match now splits on either separator, so a Windows path stops being read as one long name. Red then green pasted below; one reviewer finding argued down.

files.change: split on either separator before matching a suffix
a backslash path and a POSIX path in the same fixture

red.note: the backslash case returned the whole path as the name

review.mechanism: general-purpose subagent pointed at the auditor brief in the plugin root

items.why: no input crosses a trust boundary in this diff
no benchmark exists in this repo to run

items.text: The assertion hardcodes a forward slash, so the new case passes on POSIX and cannot fail on Windows.
The helper should raise on an empty path rather than returning an empty string.
items.reason: Two callers already treat the empty string as absent and would start crashing on a case they handle today; raising is a behaviour change nobody filed.

items.text: The docstring above the helper still describes the single-separator behaviour.

examples.split_cost: Roughly two thirds to the note (the full reviewer exchange and the caller sweep); nothing was left out of both.
